observations.statement: The core defines seven complete UI-command mappings: dev show problems, dev start session, dev stop session, Docker bake, Docker bake preview, Docker bake run, and Docker build; each names its UI location, command ID, handler location, and an empty expected_event_types list.
The three dev controls are located in Terminal and bottom runtime panels, while the Docker controls are placed at Docker Manager paths for Bake, Bake Preview, Bake Run, and Build.

Every mapping requires dispatcher registration with typed args and result, projected availability and disabled reason before dispatch, preservation of dispatch trace fields, an effect contract, and regression evidence before production certification.
Every mapping names an availability selector and disabled-reason projection under state.commands.

Every mapping declares effect_kind receipt, names a command-specific dispatch_receipt reference, states that no persisted event is declared, and requires either a no-persist receipt or route/open disposition.

Every control has accessibility obligations for stable role/name/description, keyboard reachability and activation when visible, visible focus with deterministic return after dispatch or error, and disabled-reason announcement to assistive technology.

The test-evidence pattern explicitly covers dispatcher routing, state projection, effect receipt or event assertion, accessibility regression, and a negative oracle against unexpected persisted domain events.

candidate_findings.title: Concrete typed payload and result contracts are absent
candidate_findings.statement: Across all seven complete mappings, the text requires typed args and results but does not identify concrete payload or result types, fields, required versus optional values, validation rules, serialization, or success and error variants; the alternative of an explicit route/open disposition is also not selected.
candidate_findings.impact: Dispatcher, handler, and test implementations can choose incompatible interfaces while satisfying only the generic prose, so the window does not provide an exact production contract.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt versus route/open behavior is unresolved
candidate_findings.statement: Each entry sets effect_kind to receipt and names a dispatch_receipt ref, but its effect and event-test prose permits either recording a no-persist command receipt or using an explicit route/open disposition; no rule selects the branch or defines the disposition and receipt schemas or durability.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can implement materially different command effects and certification tests can accept incompatible outcomes, especially for session and Docker controls.

candidate_findings.title: Session start and stop state-machine behavior is undefined
candidate_findings.statement: The start-session and stop-session mappings provide command IDs, handlers, availability and disabled selectors, and receipt-only no-event effects, but define no session states, transition preconditions or postconditions, mutual exclusion, idempotency, concurrent-dispatch handling, cancellation, or failure and recovery behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: The same UI actions can produce divergent session lifecycle behavior and availability races, with no persisted domain-event oracle to prove the resulting transition.

candidate_findings.title: Docker command capability and operation lifecycle are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: Bake, Bake Preview, Bake Run, and Build are mapped only to locations, handlers, generic typed-contract requirements, selectors, and no-event receipt effects; the window does not define whether each executes work or opens or routes, nor its inputs, output artifacts, progress, ordering, cancellation, retry, idempotency, concurrency, or failure semantics.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can disagree on core user-visible capability and operational safety while emitting evidence that conforms to the generic receipt requirements.

candidate_findings.title: Availability projection lacks dispatch-time consistency semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The mappings require projected availability and disabled reason before dispatch and name their paths, but do not define selector value types, state authority, refresh triggers, atomic revalidation at dispatch, or behavior if availability changes between render and handler invocation.
candidate_findings.impact: A control may appear enabled or disabled from stale state, and dispatch behavior can vary under concurrent state changes.

candidate_findings.title: Accessibility acceptance is not operationally exact
candidate_findings.statement: The contracts require a stable role, name, and description, keyboard activation, deterministic focus return, and disabled announcement, but do not name the actual roles or accessible strings, activation keys, focus return targets, or announcement timing and priority.
candidate_findings.impact: Different implementations can satisfy generic render evidence while presenting inconsistent or unusable accessibility behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Dispatch evidence identity and ownership semantics are undefined
candidate_findings.statement: Dispatch evidence must preserve command_id, origin, correlation_id, handler target, result, and receipt or event effect, but the window does not define field types, correlation-ID generation or uniqueness, the origin vocabulary, evidence owner or consumer, retention, or ordering.
candidate_findings.impact: Receipts may be non-interoperable and insufficient for deterministic traceability or audit correlation.

candidate_findings.title: Production-certification artifact oracle is underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The entries enumerate evidence categories and test IDs, but do not define artifact formats, producers, storage or reference conventions, pass and fail thresholds, or how render, dispatch, state, effect, and accessibility evidence must be linked into one command invocation.
candidate_findings.impact: Production certification can be asserted with incomplete or incomparable evidence bundles even when each generic evidence category is named.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: UI element IDs, UI locations, command IDs, and handler locations are explicit for all seven core mappings.
Availability and disabled-reason selector paths are explicit for every mapped command.
Each mapping explicitly names a command-specific dispatch_receipt reference and states that no persisted event is declared.
Accessibility coverage explicitly includes semantics, keyboard access, focus management, and disabled-state announcement for every control.
Dispatcher, state-projection, effect, and accessibility test categories have explicit test IDs and textual requirements in the demonstrated command evidence blocks.
Every command has an explicit negative event oracle requiring no unexpected persisted domain event.
The required dispatch trace fields are explicitly enumerated as command_id, origin, correlation_id, handler target, result, and receipt or event effect.

unknowns.statement: The concrete argument and result type definitions, validation behavior, serialization, and success and error variants are unknown within the assigned core.
The condition that selects a dispatch receipt versus a route/open disposition, and the schema and durability of either record, are unknown.
The state authority, producer, consumer, value types, and transition triggers for the availability and disabled-reason projections are unknown.
Session lifecycle states and Docker operation progress, ordering, cancellation, retry, idempotency, concurrency, and failure recovery are unknown.
Actual accessible roles and strings, supported activation keys, deterministic focus return targets, and disabled-announcement timing are unknown.
Receipt consumers, retention, ordering guarantees, correlation-ID generation and uniqueness, and the allowed origin vocabulary are unknown.
No explicit cross-reference in the assigned core identifies an external contract that resolves the missing payload, lifecycle, receipt, state-authority, or accessibility details.
